newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-MLS REVOLUTION LURE COACH RONGEN TO LEAVE TAMPA BAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MLS REVOLUTION LURE COACH RONGEN TO LEAVE TAMPA BAY.

text.p: The New England Revolution have hired Thomas Rongen as head coach, luring the Dutchman away from rivals Tampa Bay Mutiny, the Major League Soccer club announced on Tuesday.

Rongen, named MLS coach of the year in its inaugural season after leading the Mutiny to the Eastern Conference title with a 20-12 mark, replaces former Republic of Ireland international Frank Stapleton, who resigned after the season.
New England failed to qualify for the post-season tournament, finishing last in the five-team Eastern Conference with a 15-17 mark.
"I promise New England fans that we will play an attractive, attacking style they will be excited about and proud of for years to come," said 40-year-old Rongen.

Revolution general manager Brian O'Donovan would not comment on Rongen's salary, but the New York/New Jersey MetroStars had reportedly offered Rongen as much as $300,000 a year, a vast improvement over his $80,000 salary at Tampa.

Rongen was a youth player with famed Dutch side Ajax Amsterdam before moving to the United States in 1979 to play for former Dutch national team coach Rinus Michels, who was managing the Los Angeles Aztecs of the old North American Soccer League.

He has remained in the United States ever since, playing on various indoor and outdoor teams before beginning a new career track as player/assistant coach of the Fort Lauderdale Strikers of the American Soccer League in 1988.
